title: The Wilderness
lead: The wilderness (midbar), the dry land between Egypt and Canaan, is where Israel was formed, tested and fed for forty years. Prophets and Gospels return to it as a place of both judgment and new beginning.

sections.h: A place of testing and of love
sections.b: Israel enters the wilderness after the Sea of Reeds (Exodus 15:22), receives manna and the covenant there, and spends forty years in it after refusing to enter Canaan (Numbers 14:33–35). Deuteronomy reads the years as a time of testing and care: "to humble you and to test you" (Deuteronomy 8:2–4). Hosea and Jeremiah remember them as Israel's honeymoon with God (Hosea 2:14–15; Jeremiah 2:2), while Psalm 95 and Ezekiel 20 remember the rebellions. Isaiah promises a new way through the wilderness (Isaiah 40:3). John the Baptist preaches there, Jesus is tested forty days there, quoting Deuteronomy each time (Matthew 4:1–11), and Paul and Hebrews read Israel's wilderness story as a warning to the church (1 Corinthians 10:1–13; Hebrews 3:7–4:11).
